Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the fourth inning to commence! New Zealand just need 54 runs to win this Test match after a draw they faced in the first one. Tom Latham and Devon Conway will be opening for them. Kemar Roach will get the new ball in his hand to start. Away we go...
... FOURTH INNING ...

West Indies on the other hand, couldn't really get the better of the opposition's bowling unit. There were times when they had some good partnerships, but they failed to hold on to them. Brandon King, Kavem Hodge and Justin Greaves are the only batters who crossed the double digits, which basically sums up their part of the inning. Now, their bowling unit had only 56 runs to defend, which is next to an impossible task, but we have seen miracles happen in this sport. So stay tuned with us, as the fourth inning will commence in no time.

West Indies ended their second inning with a lead of 55 runs. The Kiwis' bowling unit rose up to the occasion. Kudos to the fielding department as well, because when the bowlers were struggling to get the wicket, it was because of the fielders that they got some important breakthroughs. Lastly, Jacob Duffy, you deserve a bow. What a bowling spell we just witnessed. He ended with 17.2-4-38-5 to close the inning.

OUT! IN THE AIR... TAKEN! Jacob Duffy gets the FIVE-FER and as he is walking back to the pavilion with the ball in his hand, the crowd are up on their feet to applaud the masterpiece they witnessed. Short of a length, on middle, angling in. Ojay Shields once again swings his willow to heave it to deep mid-wicket, but the ball gets big on him and gets the top edge. It loops toward the left of the deep fine leg region, where Michael Rae does well to get underneath the skier and scoops in safely. West Indies are all out with a lead of 55 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back after the Lunch break! The players are slowly marching toward the center of the park. Tevin Imlach and Justin Greaves will continue their inning. Michael Rae will bowl the first over in the second session. Away we go...
… DAY 3, SECOND SESSION …

Tevin Imlach and Justin Greaves are trying to make a sturdy partnership right now, and they will look forward to surviving another session to extend the lead. However, it is a tough task, but West Indies really need someone to step up to notch a big inning. On the other hand, the fielding of the Kiwis was on point. There was only a single fumble in the entire first session, where a sloppy fielding of Kane Williamson allowed the batters to get a couple of runs, but other than that, they were up to the mark. They will be eager to get early breakthroughs post Lunch break so that they can start their inning by tomorrow. So, refill your snacks and rejoin us by 12.40 am GMT to get the second session going!

Further on that event, the centurion from the previous Test for the Windies, Shai Hope, walked off the field in the very same over. Skipper, Roston Chase, as well, failed to put much impact on the match. Kavem Hodge was looking good on the crease and just when things got settled, a stunning catch from Will Young made him walk back to the pavilion.

LUNCH ON DAY 3! Yet another Day where New Zealand are comfortably sitting on the driver's seat before the Lunch break. West Indies trailed by 41 runs before the start of the Moving Day, where they lost one top-order batter and one nightwatchman on Day 2. Today, Kavem Hodge and Brandon King started pretty decently. They got a couple of nicks on the edge, but other than that, there were no real terrors from the Kiwi bowlers. But things started to fall off after a brilliant piece of fielding by Michael Bracewell, which dismissed Brandon King.
Fullish, around off, Justin Greaves blocks it away to the off side. That would be for Lunch on Day 3.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start with the action on Day 3! The umpires are marching toward the center of the park and so are the players. Kavem Hodge and Brandon King will be continuing their inning. Zakary Foulkes will start for the Kiwis and he has the new ball, which is just 10 overs old. Away we go...

The stage is set for a thrilling 'Moving Day' of this Test match. The West Indies will need to bat with patience and resilience to shift the momentum, while the Black Caps are looking to capitalize on their strong position. It's going to be an intense and gripping contest.

The Windies will need to channel their fighting spirit from the first Test's second innings to stay in this match. For the Black Caps, it's a straightforward game plan: apply relentless pressure with the ball and capture the remaining eight wickets swiftly. They're eager to exploit any movement or bounce the pitch offers, and if they can dismiss the visitors cheaply, they'll be in a commanding position to dictate the terms of the match and pursue a target for victory.

The West Indies will need to dig deep to turn this match around. They'll be looking to Brandon King and Kavem Hodge to anchor the innings and erase the deficit. The early loss of John Campbell and Anderson Phillip to the in-form Michael Rae and Jacob Duffy has put the Windies on the back foot, and they'll need to form substantial partnerships to stay in the game. The Kiwis' bowling attack may have lost Blair Tickner, but they're still looking potent under the Wellington skies.

The Basin Reserve is buzzing, and it's going to be an explosive Day 3 of Test cricket. The Black Caps have seized the reins, and the West Indies are facing an uphill battle. After a dominant Day 2 performance, New Zealand is in the driver's seat, with the Windies still trailing by 41 runs. The pitch is still offering something for the bowlers, and the Black Caps are itching to exploit any movement or bounce to wrap up the innings.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

That's a wrap on Day 2! The Kiwis have dominated proceedings yet again on the second day, having a lead of 41 runs and also picking two wickets. Looking forward to seeing what Day 3, or we can say the 'Moving Day' in Test cricket language, brings up. The action resumes at 10 pm GMT (previous day), with the buildup starting an hour earlier. Thanks for tuning in, cheers!

Jacob Duffy is up for a chat. He says that he felt it was a good time to bowl at the end. On being asked about the LBW review surrounding Anderson Phillip, Jacob said that he was surprised the LBW of Anderson Phillip wasn't given at first, as it looked plumb, so they decided to go upstairs and got the wicket after DRS. Duffy mentioned Mitch Hay's quiet presence behind the stumps, which didn't give away much. He reckons getting a lead is good, praising his team's decent batting effort and acknowledging a lead of 80-90 is decent. He adds that he was fit going into the game but felt a bit flat with his bowling, though he's feeling better now and is focused on taking wickets for the team. He praises Michael Rae, saying he's awesome to watch and a great all-rounder, good with both ball and bat. Ends up noting that the wicket historically gets better, but acknowledges the opposition bowled some good balls. He emphasizes the need to keep putting in good balls to get rewarded.

At the innings break, the heavy roller was called in by the West Indies, which makes the pitch hard and flat, and also gives a temporary advantage to the batting side. But still, New Zealand's bowling unit managed to bag two scalps by the end of the play with a lead of 41 runs. After the fall of the first wicket, the Windies opted for Anderson Phillip to survive the day as a nightwatchman, but he couldn't rise to the occasion.

After the Lunch break, West Indies had a dream start by getting two crucial wickets of in-form Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra in the first 15-20 minutes. But after that, the Kiwis fought back with the sturdy partnership between Daryl Mitchell and debutant Mitchell Hay, who scored his maiden half-century. But it was Anderson Phillip once again who stepped up and got the partnership broken. After that particular event, wickets started to fall one by one, but the tail-enders managed to get strings of small partnerships which extended their lead to 73 runs in the third session.

Stumps on Day 2 and what a day it was! SESSION SUMMARY - 27.4 overs, 110 runs and 6 wickets. Day 2 started well on behalf of the Kiwis with scoring at a healthy rate initially, but ultimately losing 2 crucial wickets in the first session. Tom Latham's dismissal set the tone, followed by Kane Williamson's big wicket, which was taken by Anderson Phillip. Earlier, Devon Conway's partnership with Williamson had helped the hosts score at a healthy clip, as a dropped catch by Brandon King proved costly, which let Conway off the hook.
